title: How Well Calibrated are Extreme Multi-label Classifiers? An Empirical Analysis

problem.claim: Extreme multilabel classifiers may need to estimate the actual probability that a label is relevant, not only rank candidate labels.

gap.claim: Calibration of extreme multilabel classifiers had not previously been evaluated in this field.

contributions.claim: The paper systematically evaluates calibration in XMLC across nine models from four model families and seven benchmark datasets.
The paper introduces calibration@k, such as ECE@k, to focus calibration measurement on the top-k probability mass in XMLC scenarios.
The paper reports that computationally efficient post-training isotonic regression improves calibration without sacrificing prediction accuracy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Different models can exhibit widely varying reliability plots.
Post-training calibration via computationally efficient isotonic regression enhances model calibration without sacrificing prediction accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: XMLC applies to large-label-space settings such as product recommendation, document tagging, and ad prediction.
XMLC classifiers both evaluate label worth and select candidates, while standard evaluation mainly captures relative score order.
Practical applications may require accurate relevance probabilities, motivating calibration assessment.
The paper evaluates calibration across models and datasets and proposes calibration@k because naive ECE is unsuitable for long-tailed XMC datasets.
The authors report variable reliability across models and improved calibration after isotonic regression without reduced prediction accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Naive ECE can produce meaningless results on long-tailed XMC datasets, while calibration@k focuses on the top-k probability mass.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation metrics should reflect the operational region where predictions are actually used.

application.claim: For ranked, large-label-space prediction systems, evaluate probability calibration on the most decision-relevant top-k outputs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether calibration@k is appropriate outside XMLC or other long-tailed ranking settings.

source_observation.claim: Isotonic regression reportedly improves calibration without sacrificing prediction accuracy.

interpretation.claim: Calibration can potentially be treated as a post-training adjustment separate from model-family selection for accuracy.

application.claim: Practitioners may consider post-training isotonic regression when calibrated probabilities are needed from an existing XMLC model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions, computational costs, or datasets under which this trade-off holds.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative calibration results.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated models, model families, or benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not describe the experimental protocol or implementation details for calibration@k and isotonic regression.
